extracted.intended_audience: software engineers, repository maintainers, and GitHub users involved in creating and reviewing pull requests
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for creating, managing, and reviewing GitHub pull requests, plus admin controls for review dismissal and best-practice criteria for effective reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating a pull request
rubrics_metrics.description: To start the review process, you need to create a pull request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: create a branch with your code changes and push to remote; use the PR creation flow (prompt after push or via Pull requests > New pull request); select the base branch (e.g., main) and the compare (feature) branch; provide a descriptive title and detailed description of your changes to help reviewers understand context and purpose; click Create pull request to complete the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a new branch with your code changes and push it to remote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branching isolates changes for review and is the starting point for a PR; ensure you push the branch so GitHub surfaces the prompt to create a PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill out PR details (title and description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a descriptive title and detailed description of your changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear title and detailed description help reviewers understand the context and purpose of the PR; include intent, scope, and any instructions for testing or important design decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding reviewers to a pull request
rubrics_metrics.description: Add reviewers who will evaluate your code changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigate to the PR, use the 'Reviewers' section on the right sidebar (gear icon or dropdown) to select users/teams. GitHub will notify added reviewers. Adding the right reviewers ensures appropriate expertise examines the changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing the code changes (Files changed tab)
rubrics_metrics.description: Go through the changes in the 'Files changed' tab to view diffs and add comments to specific lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inline commenting (click the plus icon next to a line) to point out issues, questions, or suggestions tied to exact code locations. Thoroughly inspect diffs rather than only high-level summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a review outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an appropriate review outcome when finishing a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: Comment (feedback without approval or blocking), Approve (changes look good/no blocking issues), Request changes (found blocking issues that must be addressed). Choose the option that matches the severity of findings to communicate next steps clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting your review
rubrics_metrics.description: After selecting an option, add any additional comments and submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contextual comments along with the chosen outcome so the author knows what to fix, why, and how to proceed; click 'Submit review' to record the decision and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtering pull requests by reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter PRs to see which require a specific reviewer's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the repository Pull requests tab, use the 'Reviewers' dropdown on the right to filter PRs by reviewer. This helps reviewers quickly find PRs assigned to them or see what others are responsible for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricting who can dismiss pull request reviews (branch protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control who can dismiss pull request reviews to maintain code quality and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository admins: go to Settings > Branches > Add rule (or edit rule), enable 'Require pull request reviews before merging', check 'Restrict who can dismiss pull request reviews', then specify users or teams allowed to dismiss reviews and save changes. This enforces stronger governance over review dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear and actionable feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific about the changes you are requesting or the issues you are pointing out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actionable feedback helps authors understand and address concerns efficiently — point to exact lines, suggest fixes, explain rationale, and prioritize issues (e.g., blocker vs suggestion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be respectful and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Code reviews are a collaborative process; provide feedback respectfully and constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a positive tone, focus on the code and outcomes rather than the author, and aim to foster a productive environment that encourages improvement and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use GitHub's review tools effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize inline commenting, review requests, and filtering features to streamline the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with GitHub's built-in tools (inline comments, review submission flow, reviewer assignment, filters) increases review efficiency and traceability; use them to structure feedback and handoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review in a timely manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly reviewing pull requests helps maintain development momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reviews reduce merge conflicts and waiting time for authors; schedule or triage reviews to keep the pipeline moving and prevent long-lived branches.
